newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean energy official, others defect to South.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean energy official, others defect to South.

text.p: A North Korean energy official has defected to South Korea along with his wife, daughter and a colleague, Seoul foreign ministry officials said on Monday.
"The four sought asylum in our country at the CIS (Commonwealth of Independent States) region," a ministry official said without giving details about when and how they left their communist homeland.
"They arrived in Seoul this morning after the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees confirmed their intention to defect," he added.
The defectors were identified as Min Mun-sik, 48, an official at North Korea's coal industry ministry, his wife, his 15-year-old daughter and Lee Song-ho, a translator at the ministry.
Min and Lee were attached to a coal joint venture in a CIS country when they sought defection to the South, another foreign ministry official said.
North Korea has been suffering from an acute energy shortage, which has forced more than 70 percent the country's factories to stay idle, according to Seoul officials.
Seoul government officials said between 40 and 50 North Koreans have defected annually since 1994, against 10 or less annually earlier.
About 50 North Korean defectors have arrived in the South so far this year, according to intelligence officials.
